import Mathlib

/-! Minimal re-check of the three refutation steps, mathlib-only (no project import), so the
core is verified independently of the slow full-file elaboration. Mirrors
`AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/HomogeneityOrbitCollapse.lean` verbatim. -/

universe u
open CategoryTheory Topology TopologicalSpace Order AlgebraicGeometry

theorem chk_isClosed_singleton_homeomorph {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] (e : X ≃ₜ X) {z : X}
    (hz : IsClosed ({z} : Set X)) : IsClosed ({e z} : Set X) := by
  have hpre : ({e z} : Set X) = e.symm ⁻¹' {z} := by
    ext w
    simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, Set.mem_preimage]
    exact ⟨fun h => by rw [h]; simp, fun h => by rw [← h]; simp⟩
  rw [hpre]
  exact hz.preimage e.symm.continuous

theorem chk_t1Space_of_orbit_of_isClosed {X : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] (z₀ : X)
    (hz₀ : IsClosed ({z₀} : Set X)) (horb : ∀ z : X, ∃ e : X ≃ₜ X, e z₀ = z) :
    T1Space X := by
  refine ⟨fun z => ?_⟩
  obtain ⟨e, he⟩ := horb z
  rw [← he]
  exact chk_isClosed_singleton_homeomorph e hz₀

theorem chk_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero_of_t1Space (X : Type*) [TopologicalSpace X] [Nonempty X]
    [QuasiSober X] [T1Space X] : topologicalKrullDim X = 0 := by
  letI : Preorder X := specializationPreorder X
  letI : PartialOrder X := specializationOrder X
  have h0 : topologicalKrullDim X = krullDim X :=
    krullDim_eq_of_orderIso (irreducibleSetEquivPoints (α := X))
  rw [h0]
  refine le_antisymm ?_ krullDim_nonneg
  rw [krullDim_nonpos_iff_forall_isMax]
  intro x y hxy
  exact le_of_eq (Specializes.eq hxy)

theorem chk_isClosed_singleton_of_section {k : Type u} [Field k] {X : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (p : Spec (.of k) ⟶ X) (hp : p ≫ f = 𝟙 _) (t : Spec (.of k)) :
    IsClosed ({p.base t} : Set X) := by
  haveI := isClosedImmersion_of_comp_eq_id _ _ hp
  have h := p.isClosedEmbedding.isClosed_range
  rwa [Set.range_eq_singleton (fun x => congrArg p.base (Subsingleton.elim _ _))] at h

-- A scheme is sober, so step 3 applies to any nonempty scheme that is T1.
example (X : Scheme.{u}) [Nonempty X] [T1Space X] : topologicalKrullDim X = 0 :=
  chk_topologicalKrullDim_eq_zero_of_t1Space _

#print axioms chk_t1Space_of_orbit_of_isClosed

name: rational-orbit-cannot-cover-a-scheme
description: A uniformity hypothesis of the form "every point is a translate by a base-section" silently assumes T1, hence dimension 0
metadata:

---

A homogeneity hypothesis quantified over ALL points of a scheme but supplied by
translations indexed by **rational sections** (`𝟙_ (Over S) ⟶ G`) is not a weak
point-counting gap awaiting descent — it is **contradictory** for anything of positive
dimension. Translations are isomorphisms hence homeomorphisms; the identity point is closed
(a section of a morphism to `Spec k` is a closed immersion with singleton range); a
homeomorphism carries closed points to closed points. So "every point is a translate of the
identity" forces every point closed = `T1`, and a nonempty **sober** `T1` space has
`topologicalKrullDim = 0`.

**Why:** in AJC (run 0067, 2026-07-29) this shape was the "honest gap" of the
`dim Pic⁰ = g` reduction across four sessions and three docstring sites, priced as cheap
over `k̄` and a descent question in general. It made the leg's capstone
(`isAbelianVariety_of_dimension_genus`) vacuous exactly on the `g ≥ 1` curves the leg exists
for. The tell was already in the same project: the sibling irreducibility proof translates
through closed points and then needs **Jacobson density** to "sweep up the non-closed
points" — the step an orbit cannot supply.

**How to apply:** when a uniformity hypothesis is indexed by sections over the base, ask
which points it can reach before pricing it. Use a **cover** (`ZeroHypercover`, opens) rather
than an orbit of points — AJCR's `smoothOfRelativeDimension_of_translation_cover` has the
right shape. To transport a local invariant to non-closed points you need an
extension-valued translation or a density argument, never a rational orbit. Related:
[[absence-claims-need-the-whole-project]], [[prescriptions-need-auditing-like-measurements]],
[[caveat-passes-fix-the-weak-phrase]].
